summary: At just 2.1 square miles, East Foothills isn't technically a city — it's a census-designated place tucked against the western slopes of the Diablo Range on the eastern edge of San José, and that geography is the whole story. The terrain tilts upward toward Alum Rock Park, one of California's oldest municipal parks, which means many properties sit on hillsides with unobstructed westward views across the Santa Clara Valley floor — sunset panoramas that in most Bay Area markets would push prices well past what you see here. And yet "what you see here" is still a median home value north of $1.2 million, which even against a remarkably high median household income of roughly $189,000 yields a price-to-income ratio above 6:1 — comfortable for dual-income households already holding equity, punishing for first-time buyers. Rents at $3,247 per month absorb roughly 21% of that median income, a ratio that looks almost gentle by Silicon Valley standards. The area functions as a bedroom community; major tech and healthcare employers cluster miles west along the 101 corridor and in north San José, so commuting is the default. Daily highs averaging 70°F with nearly ten hours of sunshine make the hillside trails usable year-round, but the street grid is fragmented by elevation changes and arterial roads, limiting casual walkability. East Foothills is essentially a hillside suburb grafted onto a valley metropolis — the views are earned, but so is every errand.
